subject: HIPAA discovery: BAA availability & deployment eligibility — next steps
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@cardioworks.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: gwen.park@cardioworks.com
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap from earlier — BAA & hosting questions

Hi Marcus / Marissa,

Thanks for the demo earlier — that was helpful. Quick recap from our side and two asks so we can move this through legal/procurement:

Summary of our requirements:
- CardioWorks will be processing limited patient identifiers and unstructured clinician notes for inference (PHI).
- We need a signed BAA before any production traffic containing PHI.
- We prefer a managed option but need clarity on which hosting modes Redwood supports for PHI handling (hosted API vs dedicated pools vs VPC/private).

Immediate asks:
1) Does Redwood provide a BAA standard offering? If so, which deployment modes are covered out-of-the-box vs requiring enterprise/private contracts?
2) Can you kick off the vendor security questionnaire so our security team can start reviewing? I attached the questionnaire we usually fill.

Attachments: CardioWorks_Security_Questionnaire.pdf

Next steps from us: Gwen (cc'd) will collect legal/procurement availability once we get your answers; happy to schedule a short follow-up next week.

Best,
Alex Rivera
Head of Data & Integrations
CardioWorks
From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@cardioworks.com>, Gwen Park <gwen.park@cardioworks.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 17:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap from earlier — BAA & hosting questions

Alex / Gwen — thanks for the clear recap and for sending the questionnaire. High-level answers below; I'll flag details for follow-up and a couple of action items.

High-level:
- BAA: Redwood offers a standard BAA for customers processing PHI. The BAA is available for Dedicated and Private (VPC / on-prem) deployments as part of our enterprise package. For customers on our shared hosted tier, PHI processing is not permitted under the standard hosted plan. We can discuss carve-outs but they typically require dedicated capacity or private deployments plus specific contractual terms and security review.

- Eligible deployment modes for PHI: Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) and Private (VPC or on-prem) are the supported paths. Dedicated gives managed infrastructure with tenant isolation and auditability; Private gives full customer-managed networking and HSM/KMS integrations.

- SOC 2 / security posture: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II in scope for hosted and Dedicated control planes; Private deployments transfer certain control responsibilities to the customer (e.g., network controls). We will provide our SOC 2 report under an NDA and can complete your vendor questionnaire to provide the rest of the evidence.

Action items / next steps:
1) I'll share a draft BAA (attachment) for your legal team to review — see link below.
2) We're happy to start the vendor security questionnaire. Marissa will be the primary owner for technical/security Qs; Rishi will cover ops/SRE questions.
3) Can you confirm whether CardioWorks requires customer-managed KMS/HSM, or if our managed KMS (with customer key controls) meets your needs? That will influence Private vs Dedicated recommendations.

Attachments: BAA_Draft_Redwood.docx
Related link: https://redwood-internal.company/drive/BAA-Draft-CardioWorks

Propose we schedule a 30min follow-up next week (agenda: go over questionnaire approach, clarify KMS requirement, and procurement timeline). Is Wed 5/19 or Thu 5/20 morning PT better for you?

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@cardioworks.com>, Gwen Park <gwen.park@cardioworks.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 18:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap from earlier — BAA & hosting questions

Alex / Gwen — quick technical clarifications to supplement Marcus's note:

- Data flow and PHI boundaries: For Dedicated, PHI may be processed in the reserved GPU pool; we retain KV caches for performance but provide options to disable persistent caching for PHI workloads. For Private (VPC/on-prem) all storage and keys reside in customer-controlled networks and KMS.

- Logging and auditability: We support per-request audit logs and token-level tracing; when PHI is in scope, audit retention and log export to your SIEM can be configured as part of the Dedicated/Private onboarding.

- Encryption: In transit TLS 1.2+ and at-rest AES-256; for Private we integrate with customer KMS/HSM.

- Proof points: we'll attach our SOC 2 summary and sample audit log schema in the questionnaire answers. Rishi will own the SOC 2 evidence package.

I'll start filling the vendor questionnaire and will drop partial answers into the Doc so your security/legal team can review ahead of the meeting.

Notes / open asks for CardioWorks:
- Please confirm whether you need a managed KMS with customer-supplied keys (we support both),
- Any minimum data residency or region requirements?
- Procurement timeline / target go-live (approx).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Technical Lead, Customer Security (Redwood Inference)
From: Gwen Park <gwen.park@cardioworks.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@cardioworks.com>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap from earlier — BAA & hosting questions

Thanks Marcus / Marissa — very helpful. A couple quick clarifications and next steps from CardioWorks legal/procurement: 

1) For KMS: we prefer customer-managed keys (BYOK) for PHI initially; if Redwood supports customer-supplied keys in Dedicated that would be ideal.
2) Region: US-only data residency is required for PHI.
3) Procurement timeline: our legal team wants a redline-ready BAA and about 2–3 weeks to review after we receive the draft. We can start the vendor questionnaire in parallel; please populate the high-risk control sections first (SOC 2, encryption, access controls, audit retention).

Also: we're interested in a short sandbox / POC on Dedicated for 2 weeks to validate integration (ingest + inference) before committing to a larger reserved contract. Is that something Redwood can offer (trial reserved capacity or a short-term Dedicated pilot)? If yes, please include rough pricing/credits estimates in the proposal.

I'll attach a one-page procurement checklist after I hear back on the above. For now, can you: (a) confirm BYOK support on Dedicated, (b) share SOC 2 report under NDA, and (c) start the questionnaire with the sections Marissa mentioned?

Best,
Gwen Park
VP, Legal & Procurement
CardioWorks
